transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Time: 14:30 - 15:15 UTC (45m)
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Dana (HelioFrame Head ML), Omar (HelioFrame Platform), Priya (Product), Ethan (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
- Reviewed pilot scorecard (precision/recall thresholds) and recent drift on nightly traffic.
- Discussed prompt ensembles, guardrail tightening, and a rollback/canary plan.
- Agreed next steps: share scorecard CSV, run additional evals, schedule Dedicated latency run, security follow-up.

Topics: scorecard trends, prompt set surgery, false-positive hunt, guardrail thresholds, deployment fallback plan, security/compliance checklist.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: alright hey everyone thanks for joining, um we have about 45 minutes, we'll try to cover the scorecard and then do a microsurgery on the prompts and a quick ops checklist for guardrails and rollback, is that good?
[00:12] Dana: yep that's great, thanks Maya. quick note, Priya had to step in for a few mins but she'll stay on.
[00:22] Liam: hi all, I'm Liam, i'll take the scoring section first, pulled the run from last night the eval run - so i'll screen share after this, but quick high level we saw precision drop on the clinical-entity extraction task from .92 to .82 on the 2k sample which is, yeah, not great.
[00:40] Omar: is that across all locales or just US? we had some weird tokenization on non-ascii i think.
[00:48] Liam: mostly US, a few utf-8 names got mangled, and a handful look like prompt drift where the context injection regresses scoring.
[00:58] [crosstalk]
[01:02] Dana: we started seeing it after you rolled the LM variant with the new system prompt on 12/02, do you think it's model drift or prompt mismatch?
[01:12] Liam: early look is prompt mismatch + a small distribution shift, like the templates used in production included some shorthand that the new variant interprets differently. also kv-cache warmup was lower on the nightly sim so that may have affected continuity.
[01:28] Maya: can you explain "kv-cache warmup" in simple ops terms for the product folks?
[01:32] Liam: sure, so the K-V cache note from the runtime, the first few calls after a cold start have lower context continuity. in the transcript output that manifests as dropped entity continuity, so scoring dips until cache warmed. sometimes we see that when batch size or micro-batching config changes. redwood runtime logs show cold-start count spiked on the 2am jobs.
[01:50] Priya: right - so product question: how much of this is solvable by prompt surgery vs infra config?
[01:56] Liam: both. short term we can do prompt surgery: constrain the system prompt, add explicit instruction to prefer canonical names, and add negative examples. mid-term, infra changes: adjust batching window and pre-warm cache for hot shards.
[02:10] Dana: about guardrails - last week we saw a false positive where the system flagged a benign patient note as sensitive, that triggered a manual review backlog. can we tune the safety threshold without increasing false negatives?
[02:22] Maya: that's the balancing act, yeah - we'll look at the scorecard ROC curve and pick a point that minimizes human review load while staying above your FN tolerance. can you remind us of the allowed FN rate?
[02:33] Ethan: security says FN must be < 0.5% for PHI escapes; the team can tolerate up to 4% extra manual review.
[02:42] Maya: ok noted, we'll use that as the constraint.
[02:45] [00:03:00] Liam: quick detour on metrics — we added a new per-prompt delta metric that shows how each prompt variant moves precision/recall. for this run, prompt variant B reduced recall by ~6 points but increased precision, so it's a tradeoff.
[03:10] Dana: variant B is the one that removed the legacy clarifying question, right?
[03:14] Liam: yep. removing the clarifier removed context anchoring, so model hallucinated more.
[03:20] Priya: so prompt microsurgery plan?
[03:23] Maya: propose: create 3 prompt tiers - conservative (highest precision, more clarifying Qs), balanced, and recall-optimized. we'll run the ensemble where conservative acts as a post-filter (rule + model confidence).
[03:38] Omar: routing question — can we route high-sensitivity docs to Dedicated or Private lanes? we want to keep most traffic in hosted for cost but sensitive flows in a private VPC.
[03:47] Liam: yes, routing by policy is supported. note that Dedicated has slightly lower cold-start rate on our tests because of pinned pools, but you'll pay reserved capacity.
[03:58] Ethan: security: we need KMS integration and audit logs for any PII-handling path, and SAML SSO for access. do you have SOC 2 docs?
[04:08] Maya: yes, we'll share SOC2 Type 2 and a compliance packet. we also support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated.
[04:16] Ethan: good, please send contact for compliance ops.
[04:19] Maya: action item.
[04:22] [00:06:00] Liam: back to scorecard — i'll walk through three failing examples. first case: patient note with shorthand "pt c/o sob" model expanded incorrectly to something unrelated. transcription sometimes shows that as "p t see oh b" which is an artifact.
[04:40] Dana: yeah those token splits are a pain. can we normalize shorthand upstream?
[04:44] Liam: yes, we can add a preprocessing step to normalize common clinical abbreviations before prompt. that'll likely recover 2-3 points of recall.
[04:52] Priya: what's the ETA on that?
[04:54] Omar: platform can add a small normalizer lambda in front of the inference endpoint, low effort.
[04:59] Maya: add that as an item for Omar.
[05:02] [00:09:00] Dana: regarding the false-positive backlog, is there a way to prioritize manual reviews by confidence score? we don't want to triage all of them equally.
[05:12] Liam: absolutely, add a confidence bucket: low/med/high with rules. low confidence -> manual review first; high confidence -> auto-accept. we can include that in the payload with a confidence score.
[05:23] Priya: love that. will reduce reviewer load.
[05:26] [00:12:00] Maya: ok let's lay out the tactical plan: 1) prompt surgery - create 3 tiers and run A/B on 2k evals; 2) preprocessing normalizer for abbreviations; 3) adjust batching/warmup and run Dedicated latency sim; 4) guardrail threshold adjustment and confidence bucketing; 5) security follow-up.
[05:47] Dana: that's a lot, we should prioritize. which of these gives most impact quickly?
[05:52] Liam: prompt surgery + normalizer = fastest wins. infra and Dedicated sim are important but longer lead.
[05:59] Maya: agree. we'll do prompt variants and normalizer as sprint-1, and infra sim sprint-2.
[06:06] [00:15:00] Omar: one ops question — if we need to rollback model variant how fast is that? do you have a canary/fallback policy?
[06:15] Liam: yes, we support zero-downtime rollbacks with weighted traffic shifts, canary windows, and automatic fallback when scorecard SLA violated. typical rollback to previous variant is under 5 minutes to change routing, but cold caches may take 10-20 minutes to warm.
[06:30] Priya: so we should expect brief hits in continuity after rollback?
[06:33] Liam: correct, small blip while kv-cache refills. we can mitigate with cache pre-warm scripts and synthetic traffic.
[06:40] [00:18:00] Dana: on evals - what exact artifacts will Redwood share? we want raw per-sample scores and the prompt diffs.
[06:48] Maya: we'll share: CSV of per-sample labels + scores, the scorecard with aggregated metrics, and a unified prompt diff (old/new) plus example failcases.
[06:57] Ethan: please redact any PII in the shared artifacts or use hashed IDs.
[07:01] Maya: yes, we'll hash identifiers.
[07:04] [00:21:00] Liam: quick note on quantization — we tested int4 for cost savings, but for this particular entity task quantization introduced a few hallucinations. recommendation: keep fp16 for sensitive NLP tasks, or do per-layer quantization profiling.
[07:21] Dana: cost is still a big concern, what's the ballpark saving if we go int4?
[07:25] Liam: roughly 2.5x token-cost reduction but riskier for fidelity; we can quantify per-model with a short benchmark.
[07:32] Priya: can we do mixed strategy - recall-sensitive flows use fp16 on Dedicated, bulk flows use int4 on hosted?
[07:38] Maya: yes routing policy can do that. we'll map data sensitivity tag -> model/compute profile.
[07:44] [00:24:00] Omar: about network egress — if we keep data in our VPC do you still process in Redwood infra or do we have to do Private? trying to understand data residency.
[07:54] Maya: for true data-residency you should use Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane; Dedicated with VPC peering keeps data in your region but customer data will transit Redwood-managed infra unless Private is chosen. we'll send a diagram.
[08:06] Ethan: also need to confirm logs/audit retention and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM via syslog.
[08:12] Sofia: yes audit logs and event streams can be routed; retention is configurable depending on package. we'll include details in the compliance packet.
[08:19] [00:27:00] Dana: ok quick sanity check - what's the proposed timeline if we do prompt surgery first?
[08:25] Maya: proposed: prompt variants out by 12/10, HelioFrame runs evals by 12/14, review and pick tier by 12/16, prompt deploy canary 12/20, Dedicated latency benchmark week of 12/20-12/24.
[08:38] Omar: platform resources from our side will be limited during 12/13-12/16 but we can prioritize the eval run.
[08:44] [00:30:00] Priya: small UX question — when a sample is flagged for manual review, can reviewers see which prompt generated the flag?
[08:52] Liam: yep payload will include prompt_id, prompt_text (redacted if needed), model_variant, and confidence score.
[08:59] Priya: great.
[09:02] [00:33:00] Maya: let's capture the high-risk failcases in a shared doc; we'll triage top 25 by frequency and impact.
[09:09] Dana: agreed. we'll export from our internal bug tracker and share a pick list.
[09:13] Omar: I'll attach the network peering doc and a sample VPC policy.
[09:18] Maya: action items recap: Maya to share scorecard CSV and prompt diffs; Liam to provide warmup script + quantization notes; Omar to share VPC/egress config; Ethan to point to SOC2 contact.
[09:31] [00:36:00] Dana: one more question — do you support differential privacy or data-masking at inference time?
[09:37] Liam: we don't do native DP at inference yet; we recommend token-level redaction in preprocessing for now. Private deployments can do additional HSM/KMS protections. it's on the roadmap.
[09:48] Ethan: ok note that for our compliance.
[09:50] [00:39:00] Maya: ok we're approaching the last 5 minutes. anything else urgent?
[09:55] Priya: can you also include example payload schema for the confidence buckets? that would help our integrators.
[10:00] Maya: yes will include.
[10:03] [00:42:00] Liam: lastly — small parity note: the nightly sim environment used slightly different tokenization settings; we'll align configs to match production sim exactly for the next run.
[10:14] Dana: appreciated.
[10:16] [00:44:00] Maya: thanks everyone. recap in writing and mailing the artifacts by EOD Friday 12/10. next sync? how about Wednesday 12/15 same time for a quick 30-min follow-up?
[10:28] Dana: works for us.
[10:31] Omar: works.
[10:33] Maya: great, we'll send calendar invite. thanks all.
